item.title: South Australia's Liberals face oblivion without progressive voters
item.description: The South Australian Liberals are now relying on preferences from progressives to retain a handful of seats, while Labor has commandeered the votes of those comfortable with the modern economy.

item.title: Abdel-Fattah speaks, Albanese welcomes EU boss, and Gout Gout runs
item.description: Plus: the nation's fuel supply will be in focus in federal parliament.

item.title: The collapse of Mark Zuckerberg's Metaverse is a small win, but we’ll take it
item.description: Before AI was the big tech inevitability that would proceed whether anyone wanted it or not, there was the Metaverse.

item.title: Albanese issues new world warning as Australia scrambles to secure energy supply
item.description: The prime minister has warned that Australians should expect a long period of economic unrest amid chaotic disruptions in international fuel supplies, and a trade deal with the EU could become a reality as soon as today.

item.title: Labor’s failed detention regime reminds us why punishment is the domain of the courts
item.description: The chief justice of the High Court is not happy with the Albanese government, rejecting — for the third time — its preventative detention regime as unconstitutional.

item.title: Rupert Murdoch strikes again: Just like Iraq, his fingerprints are all over Iran
item.description: Watching three hours of Fox and Friends last night felt like 2003 and the Iraq invasion all over again.

item.title: Libs urged to shift further right after their SA wipeout. How has that gone in the past?
item.description: Are the Liberals just not right-wing enough for their voters? A near decade of consistently bad results for the Liberals in Australia give us plenty of evidence to test that theory.

item.title: Are 'left' and 'right' useful anymore or do we need a need a new political alignment?
item.description: With One Nation fracturing the right and embracing elements of left-wing policies, are 'left' and 'right' even useful anymore or do we need a different spectrum?

item.title: Copyright laws must change in AI age, claims the government. Artists say big tech should just pay under existing laws
item.description: Artists and rights holder groups have been defiant about the need to change copyright law in meetings with the office of Assistant Minister Andrew Charlton, who has been spearheading the government's push to bring AI investment to Australia.

item.title: Rita's date with Rita, scabby Sloane, and is this TikTok account a Labor psy-op?
item.description: Plus the media continues to analyse Donald Trump's apoplexy, and AUSTRAC's CEO gets matter-of-fact on gambling's embedded risks.
